To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human PD1 binds differently to the two human ligands, PDL1 and PDL2.
we modeled and compared the human PD1 pathway to its mouse counterpart, which is the most widely used model for this pathway, and we found that they are significantly different.
(i) hPD1 has two ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2, (ii) hPD1 binds to each ligand differently, and (iii) the binding modes for each ligand between human and mouse are different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanism of the human PD-1 pathway, which will help in the development of new drugs against cancer and viral infections.
the development of novel computational approaches for the design of small molecule inhibitors for cancer.
the development and application of computational approaches for the modeling of the full human PD1 pathway.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human PD1 pathway is more complex than the current crystal structures suggest.
our study provided the first detailed structural characterization of the hPD-1 pathway, which will facilitate the development of new drugs targeting this pathway for immunotherapy.
our study is a significant step towards building a full atomistic model for the hPD-1 pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to provide a structural basis for understanding the differences between the mouse and the human PD-1 pathway.
we have been able to model the hPD1 pathway, which has been the focus of many research groups, and we have provided a new insight into the hPD1 interactions with its ligands, PD-L1 and PD-L2.
we built the first full model of hPD1 and its ligands, characterized the interactions between the ligands and hPD1 and showed that hPD-1 binds to its ligands differently than its mouse counterpart.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to build more models for the immune checkpoint pathways, especially human, to better understand the molecular basis of these pathways.
we need more human crystal structures of immune checkpoints to understand and model their interactions with their ligands.
it is important to have human models to understand human biology.
